title: New Postal Products
summary:
Two federal updates could influence how your packages ship and how your roads and stations look. The Postal Regulatory Commission is reviewing several new and amended Postal Service shipping agreements and is asking for public comments by October 24, 2025. Separately, the U.S. Department of Transportation is creating a new council to advise on making transportation infrastructure more visually appealing, with nominations for members due November 21, 2025.

For shippers, the postal review covers contract changes tied to services like Priority Mail, express options, ground delivery, and international packages. Large mailers that use negotiated contracts may see updated pricing or terms, and the Commission has appointed public representatives to look out for the broader public interest. For communities and travelers, the new transportation council aims to lift the look and feel of highways, bridges, and transit hubs, while keeping safety and efficiency in view. It will bring together architects, landscape designers, planners, engineers, artists, preservation voices, and government representatives to share best practices and advise on funding priorities.

There are potential downsides to watch. Smaller businesses that don’t have their own postal contracts might not benefit from the same pricing flexibility as larger shippers, and contract changes can create uncertainty in the short term. On the infrastructure front, a greater focus on aesthetics could add costs or introduce subjective choices that not everyone agrees with, and some may worry it could complicate project delivery even if safety and operations remain the priority.

If you want to weigh in, the Postal Regulatory Commission is inviting comments on the current set of shipping agreements through October 24 on its website. If you or someone you know has relevant experience in design, engineering, planning, preservation, or community advocacy, the Transportation Department is accepting brief nomination packages for the new council through November 21.
